review.title: Battery defined
review.plain: Defines battery as any willful and unlawful use of force or violence upon the person of another; it sets no punishment itself.

review.title: Battery punishments
review.plain: Battery is a misdemeanor punishable by up to six months in county jail; battery on certain officers, with injury, with serious bodily injury, or on partners is punished more, up to four years under Section 1170(h) sentencing.
acts: A battery is punishable
a battery is committed against the person of a peace officer
a battery is committed against a custodial officer
a battery is committed against any person and serious bodily injury is inflicted on the person
a battery is committed against a spouse

crimes.act: Commits a battery

penalties.penalty: A fine not exceeding two thousand dollars ($2,000), or imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding six months, or both that fine and imprisonment

crimes.act: Commits a battery against a peace officer, custodial officer, firefighter, emergency medical technician, lifeguard, security officer, custody assistant, process server, traffic officer, code enforcement officer, animal control officer, search and rescue member, probation department nonsworn employee, physician, nurse, or hospital emergency department health care worker
conditions: The victim is engaged in the performance of their duties, whether on or off duty, or as otherwise described in this subdivision

penalties.penalty: A fine not exceeding two thousand dollars ($2,000), or imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding one year, or both that fine and imprisonment

knowledge: Knowing or reasonably should know that the victim is one of the listed persons

crimes.act: Commits a battery against a custodial officer, firefighter, emergency medical technician, lifeguard, process server, traffic officer, animal control officer, nonsworn employee of a probation department, physician, or nurse
conditions: The victim is engaged in the performance of their duties, whether on or off duty, or rendering emergency medical care
An injury is inflicted on that victim

penalties.penalty: A fine of not more than two thousand dollars ($2,000), by imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding one year, or by both that fine and imprisonment, or by imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170 for 16 months, or two or three years

knowledge: Knowing or reasonably should know that the victim is one of the listed persons
terms: "Injury": any physical injury which requires professional medical treatment

crimes.act: Commits the battery specified in paragraph (1) against a peace officer
conditions: The peace officer is engaged in the performance of their duties, whether on or off duty
An injury is inflicted on that victim

penalties.penalty: A fine of not more than ten thousand dollars ($10,000), or imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding one year or pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170 for 16 months, or two or three years, or both that fine and imprisonment

knowledge: Knowing or reasonably should know that the victim is a peace officer engaged in the performance of their duties
terms: "Injury": any physical injury which requires professional medical treatment

crimes.act: Commits a battery against any person that inflicts serious bodily injury
conditions: Serious bodily injury is inflicted on the person

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding one year or imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170 for two, three, or four years

terms: "Serious bodily injury": a serious impairment of physical condition, including, but not limited to, the following: loss of consciousness; concussion; bone fracture; protracted loss or impairment of function of any bodily member or organ; a wound requiring extensive suturing; and serious disfigurement

crimes.act: Commits a battery against a spouse, a person with whom the defendant is cohabiting, a person who is the parent of the defendant's child, former spouse, fiance or fiancee, or a person with whom the defendant currently has, or has previously had, a dating or engagement relationship

penalties.penalty: A fine not exceeding two thousand dollars ($2,000), or imprisonment in a county jail for a period of not more than one year, or both that fine and imprisonment

penalties.if: probation is granted or the sentence is suspended and the person has been previously convicted of a violation of this subdivision or Section 273.5
penalties.penalty: Imprisoned for not less than 48 hours in addition to the probation conditions; the court, upon a showing of good cause, may elect not to impose it

consequences: If probation is granted, or the execution or imposition of the sentence is suspended, the defendant must participate in, for no less than one year, and successfully complete, a batterer's treatment program, or if none is available, another appropriate counseling program designated by the court

On probation, conditions may include, in lieu of a fine, payments to a domestic violence shelter-based program, up to a maximum of five thousand dollars ($5,000), or reimbursing the victim for reasonable costs of counseling and other reasonable expenses
The court shall determine the defendant's ability to pay
terms: "Dating relationship": frequent, intimate associations primarily characterized by the expectation of affectional or sexual involvement independent of financial considerations

review.title: Battery on a custodial officer
review.plain: Battery on a custodial officer who is performing their duties, where the offender knows or should know it, is punished by imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170.
acts: a battery is committed against the person of a custodial officer

crimes.act: Commits a battery against the person of a custodial officer
conditions: The custodial officer is engaged in the performance of his or her duties

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170

knowledge: Knowing or reasonably should know that the victim is a custodial officer engaged in the performance of his or her duties

review.title: Battery on school, park, or hospital grounds
review.plain: Battery on school property, park property, or hospital grounds is punishable by a fine up to $2,000, county jail up to one year, or both.
acts: a battery is committed on school property, park property, or the grounds of a public or private hospital, against any person

crimes.act: Commits a battery against any person on school property, park property, or the grounds of a public or private hospital
exceptions: Conduct arising during the course of an otherwise lawful labor dispute

penalties.penalty: A fine not exceeding two thousand dollars ($2,000), or imprisonment in the county jail not exceeding one year, or both the fine and imprisonment

consequences: When committed by a minor on school property, the court may order the minor to attend counseling at the expense of the minor's parents
terms: "Hospital": a facility for the diagnosis, care, and treatment of human illness that is subject to, or specifically exempted from, the licensure requirements of Chapter 2 (commencing with Section 1250) of Division 2 of the Health and Safety Code
"Park": any publicly maintained or operated park, not including any facility when used for professional sports or commercial events

review.title: Battery on an elder or dependent adult
review.plain: Battery on an elder or dependent adult, knowing of that status, is punishable by a fine up to $2,000, county jail up to one year, or both.
acts: a battery is committed against the person of an elder or a dependent adult

crimes.act: Commits a battery against the person of an elder or a dependent adult

penalties.penalty: A fine not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000), or imprisonment in a county jail not to exceed one year, or both that fine and imprisonment

knowledge: With knowledge that he or she is an elder or a dependent adult

review.title: Battery on transportation workers or passengers
review.plain: Battery on a public transportation operator, driver, passenger, agent, or employee is punishable by up to a $10,000 fine and a year in county jail, or state prison for 16 months to three years if injury results.
acts: a battery is committed against the person of an operator, driver, or passenger on a bus

crimes.act: Commits a battery against the person of an operator, driver, or passenger on a bus, taxicab, streetcar, cable car, trackless trolley, or other motor vehicle used for the transportation of persons for hire, or against a schoolbus driver, station agent or ticket agent, public transportation provider, or employee or contractor of a public transportation provider
conditions: The victim, in the case of an operator, driver, agent, employee, or contractor, is engaged in the performance of their duties, or is a passenger

penalties.penalty: A fine not exceeding ten thousand dollars ($10,000), or imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding one year, or both that fine and imprisonment

penalties.if: an injury is inflicted on that victim
penalties.penalty: A fine not exceeding ten thousand dollars ($10,000), or imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding one year or in the state prison for 16 months, or two or three years, or both that fine and imprisonment

knowledge: Knowing or reasonably should know that the victim is engaged in the performance of their duties, or is a passenger

review.title: Battery on public transportation property
review.plain: Battery on any person on the property or in a motor vehicle of a public transportation provider is punishable by a fine up to $2,000, county jail up to one year, or both.
acts: a battery is committed against any person on the property of, or in a motor vehicle of, a public transportation provider

crimes.act: Commits a battery against any person on the property of, or in a motor vehicle of, a public transportation provider

penalties.penalty: A fine not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000), or imprisonment in a county jail not to exceed one year, or both the fine and imprisonment

terms: "Public transportation provider": a publicly or privately owned entity that operates, for the transportation of persons for hire, a bus, taxicab, streetcar, cable car, trackless trolley, or other motor vehicle, including a vehicle operated on stationary rails or on a track or rail suspended in air, or that operates a schoolbus
"On the property of": the entire station where public transportation is available, including the parking lot reserved for the public who utilize the transportation system

review.title: Sexual battery
review.plain: Sexual battery is touching an intimate part of another, or causing another to touch, for sexual purposes against their will in specified circumstances; felony sexual battery carries up to four years in state prison.
acts: touches an intimate part of another person while that person is unlawfully restrained by the accused or an accomplice
touches an intimate part of another person who is institutionalized for medical treatment and who is seriously disabled or medically incapacitated
touches an intimate part of another person for the purpose of sexual arousal, sexual gratification, or sexual abuse

causes another, against that person’s will while that person is unlawfully restrained either by the accused or an accomplice, or is institutionalized for medical treatment and is seriously disabled or medically incapacitated, to masturbate or touch an intimate part of either of those persons or a third person
touches an intimate part of another person, if the touching is against the will of the person touched

consequences: In a felony conviction, that the defendant was an employer and the victim an employee, or that the defendant was employed at the hospital where the offense occurred and the victim was in the defendant's care or seeking medical care there, is a factor in aggravation in sentencing

crimes.act: Touches an intimate part of another person while that person is unlawfully restrained by the accused or an accomplice
conditions: The touching is against the will of the person touched

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail for not more than one year, and by a fine not exceeding two thousand dollars ($2,000); or by imprisonment in the state prison for two, three, or four years, and by a fine not exceeding ten thousand dollars ($10,000)

intent: For the purpose of sexual arousal, sexual gratification, or sexual abuse
terms: "Intimate part": the sexual organ, anus, groin, or buttocks of any person, and the breast of a female
"Touches": physical contact with the skin of another person whether accomplished directly or through the clothing of the person committing the offense

crimes.act: Touches an intimate part of another person who is institutionalized for medical treatment and who is seriously disabled or medically incapacitated
conditions: The touching is against the will of the person touched

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail for not more than one year, and by a fine not exceeding two thousand dollars ($2,000); or by imprisonment in the state prison for two, three, or four years, and by a fine not exceeding ten thousand dollars ($10,000)

intent: For the purpose of sexual arousal, sexual gratification, or sexual abuse
terms: "Intimate part": the sexual organ, anus, groin, or buttocks of any person, and the breast of a female
"Touches": physical contact with the skin of another person whether accomplished directly or through the clothing of the person committing the offense
"Seriously disabled": a person with severe physical or sensory disabilities
"Medically incapacitated": a person who is incapacitated as a result of prescribed sedatives, anesthesia, or other medication
"Institutionalized": a person who is located voluntarily or involuntarily in a hospital, medical treatment facility, nursing home, acute care facility, or mental hospital

crimes.act: Touches an intimate part of another person
conditions: The victim is at the time unconscious of the nature of the act because the perpetrator fraudulently represented that the touching served a professional purpose

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail for not more than one year, and by a fine not exceeding two thousand dollars ($2,000); or by imprisonment in the state prison for two, three, or four years, and by a fine not exceeding ten thousand dollars ($10,000)

intent: For the purpose of sexual arousal, sexual gratification, or sexual abuse
terms: "Intimate part": the sexual organ, anus, groin, or buttocks of any person, and the breast of a female
"Touches": physical contact with the skin of another person whether accomplished directly or through the clothing of the person committing the offense

crimes.act: Causes another, against that person's will, to masturbate or touch an intimate part of either of those persons or a third person
conditions: The person is unlawfully restrained either by the accused or an accomplice, or is institutionalized for medical treatment and is seriously disabled or medically incapacitated

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail for not more than one year, and by a fine not exceeding two thousand dollars ($2,000); or by imprisonment in the state prison for two, three, or four years, and by a fine not exceeding ten thousand dollars ($10,000)

intent: For the purpose of sexual arousal, sexual gratification, or sexual abuse
terms: "Intimate part": the sexual organ, anus, groin, or buttocks of any person, and the breast of a female
"Touches": physical contact with the skin of another person whether accomplished directly or through the clothing of the person committing the offense

crimes.act: Touches an intimate part of another person, or causes another to masturbate or touch an intimate part of either of those persons or a third person
conditions: The touching or act is against the will of the person

penalties.penalty: Misdemeanor sexual battery: a fine not exceeding two thousand dollars ($2,000), or imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding six months, or both that fine and imprisonment

penalties.if: the defendant was an employer and the victim was an employee of the defendant
penalties.penalty: A fine not exceeding three thousand dollars ($3,000), by imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding six months, or by both that fine and imprisonment

intent: For the specific purpose of sexual arousal, sexual gratification, or sexual abuse
consequences: Any fine amount above two thousand dollars ($2,000) is transmitted to the State Treasury for distribution to the Civil Rights Department, but not until all fines, including any restitution fines, have been paid in full
terms: "Intimate part": the sexual organ, anus, groin, or buttocks of any person, and the breast of a female
"Touches": physical contact with another person, whether accomplished directly, through the clothing of the person committing the offense, or through the clothing of the victim

crimes.act: Commits a violation of subdivision (a), (b), (c), or (d) against a minor
conditions: The victim is a minor
The person has a prior felony conviction for a violation of this section

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a felony, punishable by imprisonment in the state prison for two, three, or four years and a fine not exceeding ten thousand dollars ($10,000)

terms: "Minor": a person under 18 years of age

review.title: Arrest for school assault or battery
review.plain: Allows a peace officer to arrest without a warrant for an assault or battery on school property during school activities, and defines school.

review.title: Battery on a school employee
review.plain: Battery on a school employee, knowing of that status, is punishable by county jail up to one year or a $2,000 fine; with injury, it may be punished under Section 1170(h) for 16 months to three years.
acts: a battery is committed against a school employee engaged in the performance of his or her duties

crimes.act: Commits a battery against a school employee
conditions: The victim is engaged in the performance of his or her duties, or the battery is in retaliation for an act performed in the course of his or her duties, whether on or off campus, during the schoolday or at any other time
exceptions: Conduct arising during the course of an otherwise lawful labor dispute

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding one year, or a fine not exceeding two thousand dollars ($2,000), or both the fine and imprisonment

penalties.if: an injury is inflicted on the victim
penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail for not more than one year, or a fine of not more than two thousand dollars ($2,000), or imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170 for 16 months, or two or three years

knowledge: Knowing or reasonably should know that the victim is a school employee

review.title: Battery on a highway worker
review.plain: Battery on a highway worker who is performing their duties, where the offender knows or should know it, is punishable by a fine up to $2,000, county jail up to one year, or both.
acts: a battery is committed against the person of a highway worker

crimes.act: Commits a battery against the person of a highway worker
conditions: The highway worker is engaged in the performance of his or her duties

penalties.penalty: A fine not exceeding two thousand dollars ($2,000), or imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding one year, or both that fine and imprisonment

knowledge: Knowing or reasonably should know that the victim is a highway worker engaged in the performance of his or her duties
terms: "Highway worker": an employee of the Department of Transportation, a contractor or employee of a contractor while working under contract with the Department of Transportation, an employee of a city, county, or city and county, a contractor or employee of a contractor while working under contract with a city, county, or city and county, or a volunteer as defined in Section 1720.4 of the Labor Code who performs maintenance, repair, or construction of, or operates equipment on, or performs related maintenance work on, state highway or local street or road infrastructures in work zones

review.title: Battery on a juror
review.plain: A party to a case who commits a battery on a juror or alternate juror is punishable by a fine up to $5,000, county jail up to one year, or state prison for 16 months to three years.
acts: commits a battery against any juror or alternate juror who was selected and sworn in that legal action

crimes.act: Commits a battery against any juror or alternate juror who was selected and sworn in that legal action
conditions: The battery is committed while the legal action is pending or after the conclusion of the trial

penalties.penalty: A fine not to exceed five thousand dollars ($5,000), or imprisonment in the county jail not exceeding one year, or both such fine and imprisonment, or imprisonment in the state prison for 16 months, or for two or three years

crimes.who: A person who is a party to a civil or criminal action in which a jury has been selected to try the case

review.title: Battery on a sports official
review.plain: Battery on a sports official around an organized athletic contest, where the offender knows or should know the victim is performing duties, is punishable by a fine up to $2,000, county jail up to one year, or both.
acts: a battery is committed against a sports official

crimes.act: Commits a battery against a sports official
conditions: The battery is immediately prior to, during, or immediately following an interscholastic, intercollegiate, or any other organized amateur or professional athletic contest in which the sports official is participating

penalties.penalty: A fine not exceeding two thousand dollars ($2,000), or imprisonment in the county jail not exceeding one year, or both that fine and imprisonment

knowledge: Knowing or reasonably should know that the victim is engaged in the performance of his or her duties
terms: "Sports official": any individual who serves as a referee, umpire, linesman, or who serves in a similar capacity but may be known by a different title or name and is duly registered by, or a member of, a local, state, regional, or national organization engaged in part in providing education and training to sports officials

review.title: Interference at professional sporting events
review.plain: It is an infraction, punishable by a fine up to $250, for a spectator at a professional sporting event to throw objects on the field or court or enter the field or court without permission.
acts: Throw any object on or across the court or field of play with the intent to interfere with play or distract a player
Enter upon the court or field of play without permission from an authorized person

shared.who: A person attending a professional sporting event
terms: "Professional sporting event": a scheduled sporting event involving a professional sports team or organization or a professional athlete for which an admission fee is charged to the public
consequences: The fine is not subject to penalty assessments

crimes.act: Throw any object on or across the court or field of play

penalties.penalty: An infraction punishable by a fine not exceeding two hundred fifty dollars ($250)

intent: With the intent to interfere with play or distract a player
crimes.who: A person attending a professional sporting event

crimes.act: Enter upon the court or field of play without permission from an authorized person
conditions: The entry is any time after the authorized participants of play have entered the court or field to begin the sporting event and until the participants of play have completed the playing time

penalties.penalty: An infraction punishable by a fine not exceeding two hundred fifty dollars ($250)

crimes.who: A person attending a professional sporting event

review.title: Notice at professional sports facilities
review.plain: Requires owners of professional sports facilities to post notices with a text and phone number for reporting a violent act.

review.title: Gassing by a jail inmate
review.plain: A person confined in a local detention facility who gasses a peace officer or facility employee is guilty of aggravated battery, punishable in county jail or by two, three, or four years in state prison.
acts: commits a battery by gassing upon the person of any peace officer

crimes.act: Commits a battery by gassing upon the person of any peace officer or employee of the local detention facility

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail or imprisonment in the state prison for two, three, or four years

crimes.who: A person confined in any local detention facility
terms: "Gassing": intentionally placing or throwing, or causing to be placed or thrown, upon the person of another, any human excrement or other bodily fluids or bodily substances or any mixture containing human excrement or other bodily fluids or bodily substances that results in actual contact with the person's skin or membranes

review.title: Battery on a service member because of service
review.plain: Battery on a member of the United States Armed Forces because of their service is punishable by a fine up to $2,000, county jail up to one year, or both.
acts: commits a battery against a member of the United States Armed Forces because of the victim’s service in the United States Armed Forces

crimes.act: Commits a battery against a member of the United States Armed Forces
conditions: The battery is because of the victim's service in the United States Armed Forces

penalties.penalty: A fine not exceeding two thousand dollars ($2,000), by imprisonment in a county jail for a period not exceeding one year, or by both that fine and imprisonment

terms: "Because of": the bias motivation must be a cause in fact of the battery, whether or not other causes exist; when multiple concurrent motives exist, the prohibited bias must be a substantial factor in bringing about the battery

review.title: Battery by a jail inmate on a non-inmate
review.plain: A person confined in a city or county jail, industrial farm, or road camp who commits a battery on a non-inmate is punishable under Section 1170(h) or in county jail up to one year.
acts: commits a battery upon the person of any individual who is not himself or herself a person confined or sentenced therein

crimes.act: Commits a battery upon the person of any individual who is not himself or herself a person confined or sentenced therein

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170, or in a county jail for not more than one year

crimes.who: A person confined in, sentenced to, or serving a sentence in, a city or county jail, industrial farm, or industrial road camp in this state

review.title: Throwing acid or caustic substance
review.plain: Willfully and maliciously throwing acid, a flammable substance, or caustic chemical on another to injure the flesh or disfigure the body is punishable by two, three, or four years in state prison.
acts: places or throws, or causes to be placed or thrown, upon the person of another, any vitriol, corrosive acid, flammable substance, or caustic chemical of any nature

crimes.act: Places or throws, or causes to be placed or thrown, upon the person of another, any vitriol, corrosive acid, flammable substance, or caustic chemical of any nature
ways: causes to be placed or thrown

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for two, three or four years

intent: With the intent to injure the flesh or disfigure the body of that person
terms: "Flammable substance": gasoline, petroleum products, or flammable liquids with a flashpoint of 150 degrees Fahrenheit or less

review.title: Assault with a stun gun
review.plain: Assault on another with a stun gun or less lethal weapon is punishable by county jail up to one year or under Section 1170(h); on a peace officer or firefighter the term is up to four years.
acts: commits an assault upon the person of another with a stun gun or less lethal weapon
commits an assault upon the person of a peace officer or firefighter with a stun gun or less lethal weapon

crimes.act: Commits an assault upon the person of another with a stun gun or less lethal weapon

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail for a term not exceeding one year, or imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170 for 16 months, two, or three years

terms: "Stun gun": any item, except a less lethal weapon, as defined in Section 16780, used or intended to be used as either an offensive or defensive weapon that is capable of temporarily immobilizing a person by the infliction of an electrical charge

crimes.act: Commits an assault upon the person of a peace officer or firefighter with a stun gun or less lethal weapon
conditions: The peace officer or firefighter is engaged in the performance of his or her duties

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the county jail for a term not exceeding one year, or imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170 for two, three, or four years

knowledge: Knows or reasonably should know that the person is a peace officer or firefighter engaged in the performance of his or her duties
terms: "Stun gun": any item, except a less lethal weapon, as defined in Section 16780, used or intended to be used as either an offensive or defensive weapon that is capable of temporarily immobilizing a person by the infliction of an electrical charge

review.title: Assault with a deadly weapon or force
review.plain: Assault with a deadly weapon, firearm, or force likely to produce great bodily injury is punishable by state prison, with terms up to 12 years for machineguns or assault weapons, or on peace officers and firefighters.
acts: commits an assault upon the person of another with a deadly weapon or instrument other than a firearm
commits an assault upon the person of another with a firearm
commits an assault upon the person of another with a machinegun
commits an assault upon the person of another by any means of force likely to produce great bodily injury
commits an assault upon the person of another with a semiautomatic firearm
commits an assault with a deadly weapon or instrument, other than a firearm, or by any means likely to produce great bodily injury upon the person of a peace officer or firefighter
commits an assault with a firearm upon the person of a peace officer or firefighter
commits an assault upon the person of a peace officer or firefighter with a semiautomatic firearm
commits an assault with a machinegun

consequences: When convicted in a case involving use of a deadly weapon or instrument or firearm owned by that person, the court shall order the weapon deemed a nuisance, confiscated and disposed of

crimes.act: Commits an assault upon the person of another with a deadly weapon or instrument other than a firearm

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for two, three, or four years, or in a county jail for not exceeding one year, or a fine not exceeding ten thousand dollars ($10,000), or both the fine and imprisonment

crimes.act: Commits an assault upon the person of another with a firearm

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for two, three, or four years, or in a county jail for not less than six months and not exceeding one year, or both a fine not exceeding ten thousand dollars ($10,000) and imprisonment

crimes.act: Commits an assault upon the person of another with a machinegun, an assault weapon, or a .50 BMG rifle

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for 4, 8, or 12 years

crimes.act: Commits an assault upon the person of another by any means of force likely to produce great bodily injury

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for two, three, or four years, or in a county jail for not exceeding one year, or a fine not exceeding ten thousand dollars ($10,000), or both the fine and imprisonment

crimes.act: Commits an assault upon the person of another with a semiautomatic firearm

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for three, six, or nine years

crimes.act: Commits an assault with a deadly weapon or instrument, other than a firearm, or by any means likely to produce great bodily injury upon the person of a peace officer or firefighter
conditions: The peace officer or firefighter is engaged in the performance of his or her duties

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for three, four, or five years

knowledge: Knows or reasonably should know that the victim is a peace officer or firefighter engaged in the performance of his or her duties
terms: "Peace officer": any person designated as a peace officer in Chapter 4.5 (commencing with Section 830) of Title 3 of Part 2

crimes.act: Commits an assault with a firearm upon the person of a peace officer or firefighter
conditions: The peace officer or firefighter is engaged in the performance of his or her duties

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for four, six, or eight years

knowledge: Knows or reasonably should know that the victim is a peace officer or firefighter engaged in the performance of his or her duties
terms: "Peace officer": any person designated as a peace officer in Chapter 4.5 (commencing with Section 830) of Title 3 of Part 2

crimes.act: Commits an assault upon the person of a peace officer or firefighter with a semiautomatic firearm
conditions: The peace officer or firefighter is engaged in the performance of his or her duties

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for five, seven, or nine years

knowledge: Knows or reasonably should know that the victim is a peace officer or firefighter engaged in the performance of his or her duties
terms: "Peace officer": any person designated as a peace officer in Chapter 4.5 (commencing with Section 830) of Title 3 of Part 2

crimes.act: Commits an assault with a machinegun, an assault weapon, or a .50 BMG rifle upon the person of a peace officer or firefighter
conditions: The peace officer or firefighter is engaged in the performance of his or her duties

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for 6, 9, or 12 years

knowledge: Knows or reasonably should know that the victim is a peace officer or firefighter engaged in the performance of his or her duties
terms: "Peace officer": any person designated as a peace officer in Chapter 4.5 (commencing with Section 830) of Title 3 of Part 2

review.title: Emergency rescue personnel defined
review.plain: Defines emergency rescue personnel for use in Section 148.2.

review.title: Assault on transportation workers or passengers
review.plain: Assault with a deadly weapon or force likely to produce great bodily injury on a public transit operator, driver, agent, or passenger is punishable by three, four, or five years in state prison.
acts: commits an assault with a deadly weapon or instrument or by any means of force likely to produce great bodily injury upon the person of an operator, driver, or passenger on a bus

crimes.act: Commits an assault with a deadly weapon or instrument or by any means of force likely to produce great bodily injury upon the person of an operator, driver, or passenger on a bus, taxicab, streetcar, cable car, trackless trolley, or other motor vehicle used for the transportation of persons for hire, or upon the person of a station agent or ticket agent for the entity providing such transportation
conditions: The driver, operator, or agent is engaged in the performance of his or her duties, or the victim is a passenger

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for three, four, or five years

knowledge: Knows or reasonably should know that the victim is engaged in the performance of his or her duties, or is a passenger

review.title: Assault on a custodial officer
review.plain: Assault with a deadly weapon or force likely to produce great bodily injury on a custodial officer performing their duties is punishable by three, four, or five years in state prison.
acts: commits an assault with a deadly weapon or instrument or by any means likely to produce great bodily injury upon the person of a custodial officer

crimes.act: Commits an assault with a deadly weapon or instrument or by any means likely to produce great bodily injury upon the person of a custodial officer
conditions: The custodial officer is engaged in the performance of that person's duties

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for three, four, or five years

knowledge: Knows or reasonably should know that the victim is a custodial officer engaged in the performance of that person's duties
consequences: When convicted in a case involving use of a deadly weapon or instrument owned by that person, the court may, in its discretion, order that the weapon or instrument be deemed a nuisance, confiscated and destroyed

review.title: Assault on a school employee
review.plain: Assault on a school employee performing their duties with a deadly weapon, firearm, or stun gun is punishable by state prison, up to eight years with a firearm.
acts: commits an assault with a deadly weapon or instrument, other than a firearm, or by any means likely to produce great bodily injury upon the person of a school employee
commits an assault with a firearm upon the person of a school employee
commits an assault upon the person of a school employee with a stun gun or taser

crimes.act: Commits an assault with a deadly weapon or instrument, other than a firearm, or by any means likely to produce great bodily injury upon the person of a school employee
conditions: The school employee is engaged in the performance of his or her duties

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for three, four, or five years, or in a county jail not exceeding one year

knowledge: Knows or reasonably should know that the victim is a school employee engaged in the performance of his or her duties
terms: "School employee": any person employed as a permanent or probationary certificated or classified employee of a school district on a part-time or full-time basis, including a substitute teacher, a student teacher, or a school board member

crimes.act: Commits an assault with a firearm upon the person of a school employee
conditions: The school employee is engaged in the performance of his or her duties

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for four, six, or eight years, or in a county jail for not less than six months and not exceeding one year

knowledge: Knows or reasonably should know that the victim is a school employee engaged in the performance of his or her duties
terms: "School employee": any person employed as a permanent or probationary certificated or classified employee of a school district on a part-time or full-time basis, including a substitute teacher, a student teacher, or a school board member

crimes.act: Commits an assault upon the person of a school employee with a stun gun or taser
conditions: The school employee is engaged in the performance of his or her duties

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail for a term not exceeding one year or by imprisonment in the state prison for two, three, or four years

knowledge: Knows or reasonably should know that the victim is a school employee engaged in the performance of his or her duties
terms: "School employee": any person employed as a permanent or probationary certificated or classified employee of a school district on a part-time or full-time basis, including a substitute teacher, a student teacher, or a school board member

review.title: Hazing
review.plain: Hazing likely to cause serious bodily injury is a misdemeanor with a fine of $100 to $5,000 or county jail up to one year; hazing causing death or serious bodily injury may be a felony under Section 1170(h).
acts: engage in hazing
engages in hazing that results in death or serious bodily injury

crimes.act: Engage in hazing
conditions: The violation does not result in serious bodily injury

penalties.penalty: A misdemeanor, punishable by a fine of not less than one hundred dollars ($100), nor more than five thousand dollars ($5,000), or imprisonment in the county jail for not more than one year, or both

terms: "Hazing": any method of initiation or preinitiation into a student organization or student body, whether or not the organization or body is officially recognized by an educational institution, which is likely to cause serious bodily injury to any former, current, or prospective student of any school, community college, college, university, or other educational institution in this state; it does not include customary athletic events or school-sanctioned events

crimes.act: Personally engages in hazing that results in death or serious bodily injury
conditions: The hazing results in death or serious bodily injury

penalties.penalty: Guilty of either a misdemeanor or a felony: imprisonment in county jail not exceeding one year, or imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170

terms: "Hazing": any method of initiation or preinitiation into a student organization or student body, whether or not the organization or body is officially recognized by an educational institution, which is likely to cause serious bodily injury to any former, current, or prospective student of any school, community college, college, university, or other educational institution in this state; it does not include customary athletic events or school-sanctioned events

review.title: Shooting at an inhabited dwelling or vehicle
review.plain: Maliciously and willfully discharging a firearm at an inhabited dwelling, occupied building, vehicle, or aircraft is a felony punishable by three, five, or seven years in state prison.
acts: discharge a firearm at an inhabited dwelling house, occupied building, occupied motor vehicle, occupied aircraft, inhabited housecar

crimes.act: Discharge a firearm at an inhabited dwelling house, occupied building, occupied motor vehicle, occupied aircraft, inhabited housecar, or inhabited camper

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a felony: imprisonment in the state prison for three, five, or seven years, or by imprisonment in the county jail for a term of not less than six months and not exceeding one year

terms: "Inhabited": currently being used for dwelling purposes, whether occupied or not

review.title: Sale of vehicles used in shootings
review.plain: Requires the court to order a vehicle used in specified violent firearm offenses sold, and sets the notice, sale, and proceeds procedure.

review.title: Grossly negligent discharge of a firearm
review.plain: Willfully discharging a firearm or BB device in a grossly negligent manner that could result in injury or death is punishable by county jail up to one year, or for a firearm also under Section 1170(h).
acts: discharges a firearm in a grossly negligent manner which could result in injury or death to a person
discharges a BB device in a grossly negligent manner which could result in injury or death to a person

crimes.act: Discharges a firearm in a grossly negligent manner which could result in injury or death to a person
exceptions: Except as otherwise authorized by law

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding one year, or imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170

crimes.act: Discharges a BB device in a grossly negligent manner which could result in injury or death to a person
exceptions: Except as otherwise authorized by law

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding one year

terms: "BB device": any instrument that expels a projectile, such as a BB or a pellet, through the force of air pressure, gas pressure, or spring action

review.title: Shooting at an unoccupied aircraft, vehicle, or building
review.plain: Willfully and maliciously shooting at an unoccupied aircraft is a felony; shooting at an unoccupied motor vehicle or uninhabited building is punishable in county jail up to one year or in state prison.
acts: discharges a firearm at an unoccupied aircraft
discharges a firearm at an unoccupied motor vehicle or an uninhabited building or dwelling house

crimes.act: Discharges a firearm at an unoccupied aircraft

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a felony

terms: "Aircraft": any contrivance intended for and capable of transporting persons through the airspace

crimes.act: Discharges a firearm at an unoccupied motor vehicle or an uninhabited building or dwelling house
exceptions: Shooting at an abandoned vehicle, unoccupied vehicle, uninhabited building, or dwelling house with the permission of the owner

penalties.penalty: A public offense punishable by imprisonment in the county jail for not more than one year or in the state prison
